item.title: The Disinformation Economy: Digital Markets of Influence, Conflict, and Polarization
item.content:encoded:
Carlos Diaz Ruiz, Hanken School of Economics

Sofia Ulver, Lund University

James Pamment, Lund University

This special issue examines the intersection of digital marketing, disinformation, and societal harm. The 'disinformation economy' refers to how platform architectures and advertising technologies enable actors to profit from spreading false information, incendiary content, and polarizing material. With billions of advertising dollars inadvertently funding fake news sites and influencers potentially profiting from radicalizing content, the business models underlying digital platforms create systematic incentives for disinformation production and circulation.

The issue invites multidisciplinary research exploring how marketing technologies, algorithmic systems, and monetization schemes contribute to disinformation spread and societal polarization. It also welcomes contributions examining influence operations that exploit advertising infrastructures, as well as solutions that can inform policy, business practice, and build societal resilience against online disinformation through interventions like media literacy, fact-checking, and platform governance reforms.

Appel publié par Journal of Marketing Management. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Whether and how programmatic advertising funds fake news
  • How do the recommender algorithms amplify incendiary content
  • How can AI-generated content be used to spread disinformation
  • Do the monetization schemes of the creator economy reward polarization
  • How do influence operations exploit marketing infrastructures
  • What initiatives and interventions can strengthen societal resilience to disinformation
  • What forms of platform governance can protect liberal deliberative democracies
  • What methodologies, including Open-Source Intelligence (OSINT), can be used to investigate disinformation on AdTech and social media
